the mixing among the three states around $1\mathrm{GeV}$ and the mixing among the four states around $1.5\sim 2\mathrm{GeV}$.

the $q\bar{q}$, $s\bar{s}$ and glueball components are mixed in $f_0 (1370)$, the $q\overline{q}$ and $s\overline{s}$ components are mixed in the $f_0$ (1500), and $f_ 0$ (1710) is a glueball.

the scalar mesons $f_0$ around $1\mathrm{GeV}$ are the mixture of the $q\bar{q}$, $s\bar{s}$ and glueball, and the mixing is determined by the non-diagonal cross terms of the correlation functions in the QCD side.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can determine the fractions of the three components in the physical $f_0$ states with the QCD light-cone sum rules.
the mixing among the scalar mesons is not large and the $0^{+ +}$ glueball is not the dominant component of $f_0$ meson, which is different from the previous researches.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the QCD sum rule can be a powerful tool for mixing study.
the mixing is not a free parameter but can be determined from the first principles.
